source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 175: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Assume an authorized disposable test allocation; unknown platform facts remain unverified. Capture launcher/framework/backend, versions, image, hosts, placement, world size, timeout, and the first stalled operation. For each rank record expected/observed membership, global/local rank, PID, visible GPU, NIC/interface, rendezvous/store result, collective sequence, timestamps, exit state, and redacted logs. Check rank-set equality and ordering, device mapping, store reachability, selected routes/MTU/firewall, container device access, GPU health, topology, clock/configuration consistency, and resource headroom.

Falsifiable hypothesis: a specific rank is absent from the process group or selects an unreachable/inconsistent rendezvous or transport interface, so peers wait at initialization. Falsify it only when every expected rank joins, uses the same ordered collectives, independent authorized path checks pass, and repeated matched minimal all-reduces complete. Run a deterministic small all-reduce with a bounded watchdog and per-rank timestamps in randomized matched single-node, reduced-world, and full-world trials; hold software, placement and input constant. Measure join and first-progress latency, completion, checksum correctness, timeout/hang, rank failure, transport errors, cleanup, and success/failure denominators. Change one approved reversible interface or timeout setting at a time; preserve safety checks, stop on timeout, clean up child processes, redact secrets, and roll back after the experiment. Confounders include collective-order mismatch, stale rendezvous state, topology/NIC asymmetry, firewall/MTU, GPU or driver faults, container permissions, resource pressure, and library mismatch. Require rank logs, environment/configuration hashes, path-test results, trial matrix, and timestamps before assigning cause; this is provisional and needs domain-expert review. Scenario variant 1610 is tracked as a separate trial label; do not infer platform facts from that label.
risks: misdiagnosing a hang from incomplete rank telemetry
test-induced load or topology changes
sensitive endpoint or log disclosure
false confidence from a single successful trial
